requirements.requirement: The system must ingest raw prescribing data files (e.g., CSV/JSON) and parse them into the schema defined in EVAL-P-RX-S1 without data loss.
The system must validate each ingested record against the prescription schema and reject records that fail required field validation.
The system must normalize drug identifiers (e.g., brand/generic names, NDC codes) into a canonical drug representation.
The system must aggregate prescribing data by provider NPI and drug identifier with accurate total counts or volumes.
The system must map normalized drug records to ICD-10 conditions using the icd10_loader taxonomy.
The system must invoke an LLM-assisted mapping process when deterministic ICD-10 mapping is not available.
The system must persist normalized, aggregated, and condition-mapped prescription data to the database in the schema defined in EVAL-P-RX-S1.
The system must ensure idempotent ingestion such that re-processing the same dataset does not duplicate records.
The system must log ingestion, normalization, and mapping steps with traceable record counts at each stage.
The system must skip and log records with missing or invalid provider NPI values without terminating the pipeline.
The system must handle unmappable drug-to-condition cases by assigning a null or 'unknown' condition label and logging the event.
The system must fail the ingestion job with an error status if the input dataset is unreadable or structurally invalid.
The system must produce a deterministic output for identical input datasets given the same normalization and mapping configuration.
The system must process large datasets in batches or streaming mode without exceeding memory constraints.
The system must record confidence or provenance for LLM-assisted mappings to distinguish them from deterministic mappings.
